Passage-1
In recent times, India has grown fast not only compared to its own past but also in comparison with other nations. But there cannot be any room for complacency because it is possible for the Indian economy to develop even faster and also to spread the benefits of this growth more widely than has been done thus far. Before going into details of the kinds of micro-structural changes that we need to conceptualize and then proceed to implement, it is worthwhile elaborating on the idea of inclusive growth that constitutes the defining concept behind this Government's various economic policies and decisions. A nation interested in inclusive growth views the same growth differently depending on whether the gains of the growth are heaped primarily on a small segment or shared widely by the population. The latter is cause for celebration but not the former. In other words, growth must not be treated as an end in itself but as an instrument for spreading prosperity to all. India's own past experience and the experience of other nations suggests that growth is necessary for eradicating poverty but it is not a sufficient condition. In other words, policies for promoting growth need to be complemented with policies to ensure that more and more people join in the growth process and, further, that there are mechanisms in place to redistribute some of the gains to those who are unable to partake in the market process and, hence, get left behind.

A simple way of giving this idea of inclusive growth a sharper form is to measure a nation's progress in terms of the progress of its poorest segment, for instance the bottom 20 per cent of the population. One could measure the per capita income of the bottom quintile of the population and also calculate the growth rate of income; and evaluate our economic success in terms of these measures that pertain to the poorest segment. This approach is attractive because it does not ignore growth like some of the older heterodox criteria did. It simply looks at the growth of income of the poorest sections of the population. It also ensures that those who are outside of the bottom quintile do not get ignored. If that were done, then those people would in all likelihood drop down into the bottom quintile and so would automatically become a direct target of our policies. Hence the criterion being suggested here is a statistical summing up of the idea of inclusive growth, which, in turn, leads to two corollaries to wish that India must strive to achieve high growth and that we must work to ensure that weakest segments benefit from the growth.

समावेशी संवृद्धि के इस विचार को एक अधिक सुस्पष्ट रूप देने का एक सरल तरीका यह है कि किसी राष्ट्र की उन्नति को उसके सबसे गरीब हिस्से, उदाहरणार्थ, जनसंख्या के सबसे निचले 20%, की उन्नति के आधार पर मापा जाए। जनसंख्या के इस सबसे निचले पाँचवें हिस्से की प्रति व्यक्ति आय को मापा जा सकता है और आय की वृद्धि-दर की गणना भी की जा सकती है; और सबसे ग़रीब हिस्से से सम्बन्धित इन मापकों के आधार पर हमारी आर्थिक सफलता का आकलन किया जा सकता है। यह दृष्टि आकर्षक है, क्योंकि यह संवृद्धि की उस तरह उपेक्षा नहीं करती जैसी कि कुछ पहले के परम्पराविरुद्ध मानदण्डों में की जाती थी। यह बस जनसंख्या के सबसे गरीब हिस्से की आय की वृद्धि को ही देखती है। यह इसे भी सुनिश्चित करती है कि ऐसे लोगों की भी उपेक्षा न हो जो इस निचले पाँचवें हिस्से से बाहर हैं। अगर ऐसा हो, तो पूरी सम्भावना है कि वे लोग भी इस निचले पाँचवें हिस्से में आ जाएँ और इस प्रकार अपने-आप ही हमारी इन नीतियों का सीधा लक्ष्य बन जाएँ। इस प्रकार यहाँ सुझाए गए मानदण्ड समावेशी संवृद्धि के विचार का सांख्यिकीय समाकलन हैं जो परिणामतः दो उपसिद्धांतों की ओर ले जाते हैं: यह इच्छा करना कि आवश्यक रूप से भारत ऊँची संवृद्धि प्राप्त करने का प्रयास करे और हम इसे सुनिश्चित करने के लिए कार्य करें कि संवृद्धि से सबसे ग़रीब हिस्से लाभान्वित हों।

Directions for the following 5 (five) items: Read the following two passages and answer the items that follow each passage. Your answers to these items should be based on the passages only.

Passage-1
In recent times, India has grown fast not only compared to its own past but also in comparison with other nations. But there cannot be any room for complacency because it is possible for the Indian economy to develop even faster and also to spread the benefits of this growth more widely than has been done thus far. Before going into details of the kinds of micro-structural changes that we need to conceptualize and then proceed to implement, it is worthwhile elaborating on the idea of inclusive growth that constitutes the defining concept behind this Government's various economic policies and decisions. A nation interested in inclusive growth views the same growth differently depending on whether the gains of the growth are heaped primarily on a small segment or shared widely by the population. The latter is cause for celebration but not the former. In other words, growth must not be treated as an end in itself but as an instrument for spreading prosperity to all. India's own past experience and the experience of other nations suggests that growth is necessary for eradicating poverty but it is not a sufficient condition. In other words, policies for promoting growth need to be complemented with policies to ensure that more and more people join in the growth process and, further, that there are mechanisms in place to redistribute some of the gains to those who are unable to partake in the market process and, hence, get left behind.

A simple way of giving this idea of inclusive growth a sharper form is to measure a nation's progress in terms of the progress of its poorest segment, for instance the bottom 20 per cent of the population. One could measure the per capita income of the bottom quintile of the population and also calculate the growth rate of income; and evaluate our economic success in terms of these measures that pertain to the poorest segment. This approach is attractive because it does not ignore growth like some of the older heterodox criteria did. It simply looks at the growth of income of the poorest sections of the population. It also ensures that those who are outside of the bottom quintile do not get ignored. If that were done, then those people would in all likelihood drop down into the bottom quintile and so would automatically become a direct target of our policies. Hence the criterion being suggested here is a statistical summing up of the idea of inclusive growth, which, in turn, leads to two corollaries to wish that India must strive to achieve high growth and that we must work to ensure that weakest segments benefit from the growth.

question_english: Five persons fire bullets at a target at an interval of 6, 7, 8, 9 and 12 seconds respectively. The number of times they would fire the bullets together at the target in an hour is
question_hindi: पाँच व्यक्ति एक लक्ष्य पर क्रमशः 6, 7, 8, 9 और 12 सेकण्ड के अन्तराल पर गोलियाँ दागते हैं। एक घंटे में वे लक्ष्य पर एक साथ कितनी बार गोलियाँ दागेंगे ?
explanation_english:
Correct Answer: (b) 7
Explanation: First, find the LCM of the intervals: $\text{LCM}(6, 7, 8, 9, 12) = 504\text{ seconds}$. This means they fire together every $504$ seconds. In one hour ($3600\text{ seconds}$), the number of times they fire together after the start is $3600 / 504 \approx 7.14$, yielding 7 times.
explanation_hindi:
सही उत्तर: (b) 7
स्पष्टीकरण: सबसे पहले अंतरालों का लघुत्तम समापवर्त्य (LCM) ज्ञात करते हैं: $\text{LCM}(6, 7, 8, 9, 12) = 504\text{ सेकण्ड}$। इसका अर्थ है कि वे हर $504$ सेकण्ड बाद एक साथ गोलियाँ दागते हैं। एक घंटे ($3600\text{ सेकण्ड}$) में, कुल बार = $3600 / 504 \approx 7.14$, अर्थात 7 बार।

question_english: A group of 630 children is seated in rows for a group photo session. Each row contains three less children than the row in front of it. Which one of the following number of rows is not possible?
question_hindi: 630 बच्चों के एक समूह को सामूहिक फोटो लेने के लिए पंक्तियों में बिठाया गया। प्रत्येक पंक्ति में उसके आगे की पंक्ति की तुलना में तीन बच्चे कम थे। पंक्तियों की निम्नलिखित संख्याओं में से कौन-सी एक, संभव नहीं है ?
explanation_english:
Correct Answer: (d) 6
Explanation: Let $n$ be the number of rows and $a$ be children in the front row. The total sum is given by $\frac{n}{2}[2a - 3(n - 1)] = 630 \implies n[2a - 3(n - 1)] = 1260$. Testing option (d) $n = 6$: $6[2a - 15] = 1260 \implies 2a - 15 = 210 \implies 2a = 225$, which yields a non-integer ($a = 112.5$). Thus, 6 rows is impossible.
explanation_hindi:
सही उत्तर: (d) 6
स्पष्टीकरण: मान लीजिए पंक्तियों की संख्या $n$ है और पहली पंक्ति में बच्चों की संख्या $a$ है। कुल योग $\frac{n}{2}[2a - 3(n - 1)] = 630 \implies n[2a - 3(n - 1)] = 1260$ है। विकल्प (d) $n = 6$ रखने पर: $6[2a - 15] = 1260 \implies 2a = 225$, जो एक पूर्णांक नहीं है ($a = 112.5$)। अतः 6 पंक्तियाँ संभव नहीं हैं।

question_hindi: एक सीढ़ी पर सात व्यक्ति A, B, C, D, E, F और G (इस क्रम में नहीं) हैं। A, E से ऊपर है लेकिन C से नीचे है। B मध्य में है। G, A और B के बीच में है। E, B और F के बीच में है। यदि F, E और D के बीच में है, तो सीढ़ी के सबसे निचले सोपान पर कौन-सा व्यक्ति होगा ?

Correct Answer: (c) D
Explanation: Arranging top to bottom: B is in the middle (position 4 out of 7). G is between A and B, and A is lower than C, so top 3 are C, A, G. E is between B and F, and F is between E and D, so positions 5, 6, 7 are E, F, D. Thus, the bottom step is occupied by D.

सही उत्तर: (c) D

question_english:
Assume that
1. the hour and minute hands of a clock move without jerking.
2. the clock shows a time between 8 o'clock and 9 o'clock.
3. the two hands of the clock are one above the other.
After how many minutes (nearest integer) will the two hands be again lying one above the other?
question_hindi:
कल्पना कीजिए कि
1. एक घड़ी की घंटे व मिनट की सुइयाँ बिना झटके के चलती हैं।
2. घड़ी 8 बजे और 9 बजे के बीच का समय दिखाती है।
3. घड़ी की दोनों सुइयाँ एक-दूसरे के ऊपर हैं।
कितने मिनट (निकटतम पूर्णांक) बाद दोनों सुइयाँ फिर एक बार एक-दूसरे के ऊपर होंगी ?
explanation_english:
Correct Answer: (c) 65
Explanation: The time interval between any two consecutive coincidences of the hour and minute hands of a clock is always $\frac{720}{11} \text{ minutes} \approx 65.45\text{ minutes}$. Rounded to the nearest integer, it is 65 minutes.
explanation_hindi:
सही उत्तर: (c) 65

It is essential that we mitigate the emissions of greenhouse gases and thus avoid some of the worst impacts of climate change that would take place in coming years and decades. Mitigation would require a major shift in the way we produce and consume energy. A shift away from overwhelming dependence on fossil fuels is now long overdue, but unfortunately, technological development has been slow and inadequate largely because government policies have not promoted investments in research and development, myopically as a result of relatively low prices of oil. It is now, therefore, imperative for a country like India treating the opportunity of harnessing renewable energy on a large scale as a national imperative. This country is extremely well endowed with solar, wind and biomass sources of energy. Where we have lagged, unfortunately, is in our ability to develop and to create technological solutions for harnessing these resources.

One particular trajectory for carrying out stringent mitigation of greenhouse gas emissions assessed by the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) clearly shows the need for ensuring that global emissions of greenhouse gases peak no later than 2015 and reduce rapidly thereafter. The cost associated with such a trajectory is truly modest and would amount, in the estimation of IPCC, to not more than 3 percent of the global GDP in 2030. In other words, the level of prosperity that the world would have reached without mitigation would at worst be postponed by a few months or a year at the most. This is clearly not a very high price to pay for protecting hundreds of millions of people from the worst risks associated with climate change. Any such effort, however, would require lifestyles to change appropriately also. Mitigation of greenhouse gas emissions is not a mere technological fix, and clearly requires changes in lifestyles and transformation of a country's economic structure, whereby effective reduction in emissions is brought about, such as through the consumption of much lower quantities of animal protein. The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) has determined that the emissions from the livestock sector amount to 18 percent of the total. The reduction of emissions from this source is entirely in the hands of human beings, who have never questioned the impacts that their dietary habits of consuming more and more animal protein are bringing about. Mitigation overall has huge co-benefits, such as lower air pollution and health benefits, higher energy security and greater employment.

It is essential that we mitigate the emissions of greenhouse gases and thus avoid some of the worst impacts of climate change that would take place in coming years and decades. Mitigation would require a major shift in the way we produce and consume energy. A shift away from overwhelming dependence on fossil fuels is now long overdue, but unfortunately, technological development has been slow and inadequate largely because government policies have not promoted investments in research and development, myopically as a result of relatively low prices of oil. It is now, therefore, imperative for a country like India treating the opportunity of harnessing renewable energy on a large scale as a national imperative. This country is extremely well endowed with solar, wind and biomass sources of energy. Where we have lagged, unfortunately, is in our ability to develop and to create technological solutions for harnessing these resources.

One particular trajectory for carrying out stringent mitigation of greenhouse gas emissions assessed by the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) clearly shows the need for ensuring that global emissions of greenhouse gases peak no later than 2015 and reduce rapidly thereafter. The cost associated with such a trajectory is truly modest and would amount, in the estimation of IPCC, to not more than 3 percent of the global GDP in 2030. In other words, the level of prosperity that the world would have reached without mitigation would at worst be postponed by a few months or a year at the most. This is clearly not a very high price to pay for protecting hundreds of millions of people from the worst risks associated with climate change. Any such effort, however, would require lifestyles to change appropriately also. Mitigation of greenhouse gas emissions is not a mere technological fix, and clearly requires changes in lifestyles and transformation of a country's economic structure, whereby effective reduction in emissions is brought about, such as through the consumption of much lower quantities of animal protein. The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) has determined that the emissions from the livestock sector amount to 18 percent of the total. The reduction of emissions from this source is entirely in the hands of human beings, who have never questioned the impacts that their dietary habits of consuming more and more animal protein are bringing about. Mitigation overall has huge co-benefits, such as lower air pollution and health benefits, higher energy security and greater employment.

1. Inadequate technological development
2. Inadequate funds for research and development
3. Inadequate availability of alternative sources of energy
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
question_hindi:
हम जीवाश्म ईंधनों पर अत्यधिक निर्भर क्यों बने हुए हैं ?
1. अपर्याप्त प्रौद्योगिकीय विकास

नीचे दिए गए कूट का प्रयोग कर सही उत्तर चुनिए :

It is essential that we mitigate the emissions of greenhouse gases and thus avoid some of the worst impacts of climate change that would take place in coming years and decades. Mitigation would require a major shift in the way we produce and consume energy. A shift away from overwhelming dependence on fossil fuels is now long overdue, but unfortunately, technological development has been slow and inadequate largely because government policies have not promoted investments in research and development, myopically as a result of relatively low prices of oil. It is now, therefore, imperative for a country like India treating the opportunity of harnessing renewable energy on a large scale as a national imperative. This country is extremely well endowed with solar, wind and biomass sources of energy. Where we have lagged, unfortunately, is in our ability to develop and to create technological solutions for harnessing these resources.

One particular trajectory for carrying out stringent mitigation of greenhouse gas emissions assessed by the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) clearly shows the need for ensuring that global emissions of greenhouse gases peak no later than 2015 and reduce rapidly thereafter. The cost associated with such a trajectory is truly modest and would amount, in the estimation of IPCC, to not more than 3 percent of the global GDP in 2030. In other words, the level of prosperity that the world would have reached without mitigation would at worst be postponed by a few months or a year at the most. This is clearly not a very high price to pay for protecting hundreds of millions of people from the worst risks associated with climate change. Any such effort, however, would require lifestyles to change appropriately also. Mitigation of greenhouse gas emissions is not a mere technological fix, and clearly requires changes in lifestyles and transformation of a country's economic structure, whereby effective reduction in emissions is brought about, such as through the consumption of much lower quantities of animal protein. The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) has determined that the emissions from the livestock sector amount to 18 percent of the total. The reduction of emissions from this source is entirely in the hands of human beings, who have never questioned the impacts that their dietary habits of consuming more and more animal protein are bringing about. Mitigation overall has huge co-benefits, such as lower air pollution and health benefits, higher energy security and greater employment.

question_english: There are 50 students admitted to a nursery class. Some students can speak only English and some can speak only Hindi. 10 students can speak both English and Hindi. If the number of students who can speak English is 21, then how many students can speak Hindi, how many can only Hindi and how many can speak only English?
question_hindi: एक नर्सरी कक्षा में 50 विद्यार्थियों को प्रवेश दिया गया। कुछ विद्यार्थी केवल अंग्रेज़ी बोल सकते हैं और कुछ केवल हिन्दी बोल सकते हैं। 10 विद्यार्थी अंग्रेज़ी और हिन्दी दोनों बोल सकते हैं। यदि उन विद्यार्थियों की संख्या, जो अंग्रेज़ी बोल सकते हैं, 21 है, तो कितने विद्यार्थी हिन्दी बोल सकते हैं, कितने केवल हिन्दी बोल सकते हैं और कितने केवल अंग्रेज़ी बोल सकते हैं ?
explanation_english:
Correct Answer: (d) क्रमशः 39, 29 and 11 respectively
Explanation: Total students = 50. English speakers = 21, both = 10. Only English = $21 - 10 = 11$. Only Hindi = Total - English speakers = $50 - 21 = 29$. Total Hindi speakers = Only Hindi + Both = $29 + 10 = 39$. Thus, Hindi speakers, only Hindi speakers, and only English speakers are 39, 29, and 11 respectively.
explanation_hindi:
सही उत्तर: (d) क्रमशः 39, 29 और 11
स्पष्टीकरण: कुल विद्यार्थी = 50। अंग्रेज़ी बोलने वाले = 21, दोनों बोलने वाले = 10। केवल अंग्रेज़ी = $21 - 10 = 11$। केवल हिन्दी = कुल विद्यार्थी - अंग्रेज़ी बोलने वाले = $50 - 21 = 29$। कुल हिन्दी बोलने वाले = केवल हिन्दी + दोनों = $29 + 10 = 39$। इस प्रकार कुल हिन्दी, केवल हिन्दी और केवल अंग्रेज़ी बोलने वाले क्रमशः 39, 29 और 11 हैं।

question_hindi: छह पुस्तकों को A, B, C, D, E और F से अंकित कर एक के बगल में एक रख दिया जाता है। B, C, E और F पुस्तकों के हरे आवरण हैं जबकि अन्य पुस्तकों के आवरण पीले हैं। A, B और D पुस्तकें नई हैं जबकि शेष पुरानी पुस्तकें हैं। A, B और C पुस्तकें विधि रिपोर्ट हैं जबकि शेष पुस्तकें आयुर्विज्ञान के उद्धरण हैं। कौन-सी दो, पुरानी आयुर्विज्ञान के उद्धरणों की हरे आवरणों वाली पुस्तकें हैं ?

question_english: A straight line segment is 36 cm long. Points are to be marked on the line from both the end points. From each end, the first point is at a distance of 1 cm from the end, the second point is at a distance of 2 cm from the first point and the third point is at a distance of 3 cm from the second point and so on. If the points on the ends are not counted and the common points are counted as one, what is the number of points?
question_hindi: एक सरल रेखाखण्ड 36 cm लंबा है। इस रेखा पर, रेखा के दोनों अंत्य बिन्दुओं से बिन्दु अंकित करने हैं। प्रत्येक अंत्य बिन्दु से, पहला बिन्दु अंत्य बिन्दु से 1 cm की दूरी पर, दूसरा बिन्दु पहले बिन्दु से 2 cm की दूरी पर और तीसरा बिन्दु दूसरे बिन्दु से 3 cm की दूरी पर है और यही क्रम आगे जारी है। यदि अंत्य बिन्दुओं को न गिना जाए और, उभयनिष्ठ बिन्दुओं को 1 गिना जाए, तो बिन्दुओं की संख्या क्या है ?
explanation_english:
Correct Answer: (b) 12
Explanation: Measuring from the left end, distances are triangular numbers: $1, 1+2=3, 3+3=6, 6+4=10, 10+5=15, 15+6=21, 21+7=28$. Points from left: {1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21, 28} (7 points). Measuring from the right end, points are at: {35, 33, 30, 26, 21, 15, 8} (7 points). Common points are 15 and 21 (2 points). Total unique points $= 7 + 7 - 2 = 12$.

question_english: If Sohan, while selling two goats at the same price, makes a profit of 10% on one goat and suffers a loss of 10% on the other
question_hindi: यदि सोहन दो बकरियों को एक ही दाम पर बेचकर, एक बकरी पर 10% लाभ कमाता है और दूसरी पर 10% हानि भुगतता है, तो
option_a_english: he makes no profit and no loss.
option_a_hindi: उसे न तो लाभ होगा और न ही हानि होगी
explanation_english:
Correct Answer: (c) he suffers a loss of 1%.
Explanation: When two articles are sold at the same selling price, one at a profit of $x\%$ and the other at a loss of $x\%$, there is always a net loss given by the formula $\text{Loss } \% = \frac{x²}{100} = \frac{10²}{100} = 1\%$.
explanation_hindi:
सही उत्तर: (c) उसे 1% की हानि होगी
स्पष्टीकरण: जब दो वस्तुओं को समान विक्रय मूल्य पर बेचा जाए, एक पर $x\%$ लाभ और दूसरी पर $x\%$ हानि हो, तो सदैव हानि होती है, जिसका प्रतिशत $\frac{x^2}{100}$ होता है। यहाँ $\frac{10^2}{100} = 1\%$ की हानि होगी।

question_english: Out of a total of 120 musicians in a club, 5% can play all the three instruments, guitar, violin and flute. It so happens that the number of musicians who can play any two and only two of the above instruments is 30. The number of musicians who can play the guitar alone is 40. What is the total number of those who can play violin alone or flute alone?
question_hindi: एक क्लब के कुल 120 संगीतज्ञों में से 5% गिटार, वायलिन और बाँसुरी, तीनों वाद्य बजा सकते हैं। उपर्युक्त वाद्यों में से कोई दो और केवल दो वाद्य बजा सकने वाले संगीतज्ञों की संख्या 30 है। जो संगीतज्ञ केवल गिटार बजा सकते हैं, वे 40 हैं। ऐसे संगीतज्ञों की कुल संख्या बताइए जो केवल वायलिन बजा सकते हैं या केवल बाँसुरी बजा सकते हैं।
explanation_english:
Correct Answer: (b) 44
Explanation: Total musicians = 120. All three $= 5\% \text{ of } 120 = 6$. Exactly two instruments $= 30$. Guitar alone $= 40$. Total musicians playing guitar, violin, or flute = 120 (assuming all play at least one). Let $V$ be violin alone and $F$ be flute alone. Total $= (\text{Guitar alone}) + (\text{Violin alone}) + (\text{Flute alone}) + (\text{Exactly two}) + (\text{All three}) \implies 120 = 40 + V + F + 30 + 6 \implies 120 = 76 + V + F \implies V + F = 120 - 76 = 44$.
explanation_hindi:
सही उत्तर: (b) 44
स्पष्टीकरण: कुल संगीतज्ञ = 120। तीनों वाद्य बजाने वाले = $120$ का $5\% = 6$। केवल दो वाद्य बजाने वाले = 30। केवल गिटार बजाने वाले = 40। कुल संगीतज्ञ = (केवल गिटार) + (केवल वायलिन) + (केवल बाँसुरी) + (केवल दो वाद्य) + (तीनों वाद्य) $\implies 120 = 40 + V + F + 30 + 6 \implies V + F = 44$।

question_english: Six identical cards are placed on a table. Each card has number '1' marked on one side and number '2' marked on its other side. All the six cards are placed in such a manner that the number '1' is on the upper side. In one try, exactly four (neither more nor less) cards are turned upside down. In how many least number of tries can the cards be turned upside down such that all the six cards show number '2' on the upper side?
question_hindi: एक मेज़ पर 6 एकसमान कार्ड रखे हुए हैं। प्रत्येक कार्ड के एक फलक पर संख्या '1' व इसके दूसरे फलक पर संख्या '2' अंकित है। सभी छह कार्ड ऐसे रखे हुए हैं कि संख्या '1' वाला फलक ऊपर की तरफ है। एक प्रयास में, तथ्यतः चार (न कम और न ही उससे अधिक) कार्डों को पलटा जाता है। कार्डों को न्यूनतम कितने प्रयासों में ऐसे पलटा जा सकता है कि सभी छह कार्डों के ऊपर संख्या '2' दिखे ?
explanation_english:
Correct Answer: (a) 3
Explanation: Initial state: six '1's (even number of 1s, zero 2s). Each flip changes 4 cards. Let's track the number of '2's showing:
- Start: 0 twos
- Try 1: Flip 4 cards showing '1' to '2'. Now we have 4 twos and 2 ones.
- Try 2: Flip 3 cards showing '2' and 1 card showing '1'. (Total 4 flipped). Now we have $(4 - 3 + 1) = 2$ twos and 4 ones.
- Try 3: Flip 2 cards showing '2' and 2 cards showing '1'. (Total 4 flipped). Now we have $(2 - 2 + 4) = 6$ twos. All cards show '2'.
Thus, it takes a minimum of 3 tries.
explanation_hindi:
सही उत्तर: (a) 3
स्पष्टीकरण: प्रारंभिक स्थिति: सभी 6 कार्डों पर '1' है (यानी 0 बार '2')। प्रत्येक प्रयास में 4 कार्ड पलटे जाते हैं:
- प्रयास 1: चार '1' वाले कार्डों को पलटकर '2' बनाएं (अब 4 कार्ड '2' और 2 कार्ड '1' हैं)।
- प्रयास 2: तीन '2' वाले और एक '1' वाले कार्ड को पलटें (अब 2 कार्ड '2' और 4 कार्ड '1' हैं)।
- प्रयास 3: दो '2' वाले और दो '1' वाले कार्डों को पलटें (अब सभी 6 कार्डों पर '2' हो जाते हैं)।
न्यूनतम 3 प्रयास लगेंगे।

It is often forgotten that globalization is not only about policies on international economic relationships and transactions, but has equally to do with domestic policies of a nation. Policy changes necessitated by meeting the internationally set conditions (by WTO etc.) of free trade and investment flows obviously affect domestic producers and investors. But the basic philosophy underlying absolute globalization emphasizes freedom to markets to determine prices and production and distribution patterns, and view government interventions as processes that create distortions and bring in inefficiency. Thus, public enterprises have to be privatized through disinvestments and sales; sectors and activities hitherto reserved for the public sector have to be opened to the private sector. This logic extends to the social services like education and health. Any restrictions on the adjustments in workforce by way of retrenchment of workers should also be removed and exit should be made easier by removing any restrictions on closures. Employment and wages should be governed by free play of market forces, as any measure to regulate them can discourage investment and also create inefficiency in production. Above all, in line with the overall philosophy of reduction in the role of the State, fiscal reforms should be undertaken to have generally low levels of taxation and government expenditure should be kept to the minimum to abide by the principle of fiscal prudence. All these are policy actions on the domestic front and are not directly related to the core items of the globalization agenda, namely free international flow of goods and finance.

question_hindi: निम्नलिखित सारणी में बताया गया है कि दो छात्रों ने भिन्न-भिन्न विषयों में कितने कितने अंक प्राप्त किए (अंग्रेज़ी 60/100, 80/150; मनोविज्ञान 70/100, 70/100; इतिहास 50/100, 60/100; संस्कृत 30/50, 15/25)। छात्रों के माध्य समुच्चयी प्रतिशत अंकों में कितना अंतर है ?

Explanation: Total maximum marks for A = $100 + 100 + 100 + 50 = 350$. Total marks obtained by A = $60 + 70 + 50 + 30 = 210$. Percentage for A = $(210/350) \times 100 = 60\%$.
Total maximum marks for B = $150 + 100 + 100 + 25 = 375$. Total marks obtained by B = $80 + 70 + 60 + 15 = 225$. Percentage for B = $(225/375) \times 100 = 60\%$.
Difference $= 60\% - 60\% = 0$ (Zero).

question_english: A bell rings every 18 minutes. A second bell rings every 24 minutes. A third bell rings every 32 minutes. If all the three bells ring at same time at 8 o'clock in the morning, at what other time will they all ring together?
question_hindi: एक घंटी हर 18 मिनट पर बजती है। एक दूसरी घंटी हर 24 मिनट पर बजती है। एक तीसरी घंटी हर 32 मिनट पर बजती है। यदि सभी तीनों घंटियाँ एक ही समय में सुबह 8 बजे बजती हैं, तो दूसरे किस समय पर वे एक साथ बजेंगी ?
explanation_english:
Correct Answer: (b) 12:48 hrs
Explanation: Find the LCM of 18, 24, and 32:
- $18 = 2 \times 3²$
- $24 = 2³ \times 3$
- $32 = 2⁵$
$\text{LCM} = 2⁵ \times 3² = 32 \times 9 = 288 \text{ minutes}$.
$288 \text{ minutes} = 4 \text{ hours } 48 \text{ minutes}$.
Adding this to 8:00 AM gives 12:48 PM (12:48 hrs).
explanation_hindi:
सही उत्तर: (b) 12:48 बजे
स्पष्टीकरण: 18, 24 और 32 का लघुत्तम समापवर्त्य (LCM) = $2^5 \times 3^2 = 288 \text{ मिनट}$ यानी 4 घंटे 48 मिनट। सुबह 8:00 बजे में 4 घंटे 48 मिनट जोड़ने पर 12:48 बजे प्राप्त होता है।

question_english: A and B decide to travel from place X to place Y by bus. A has ₹10 with him and he finds it is 80% of the bus fare for two persons. B finds that he has ₹3 with him and hands it to A. In this context, which one of the following statements is correct?
question_hindi: A और B बस द्वारा स्थान X से स्थान Y तक जाने का निश्चय करते हैं। A के पास ₹10 हैं और उसे पता चलता है कि यह राशि दो व्यक्तियों के लिए बस किराए का 80% है। B के पास ₹3 मिलते हैं जिसे वह A को दे देता है। इस संदर्भ में, निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा एक कथन सही है ?
option_a_english: Now the money A has is just enough to buy two tickets.
option_b_english: A still needs ₹2 for buying the tickets.
option_c_english: After buying the two tickets A will be left with 50 paise.
option_d_english: The money A now has is still not sufficient to buy two tickets.
option_a_hindi: A के पास अब जो नकदी है, वह मात्र दो टिकटों के लिए ही पर्याप्त है।
option_b_hindi: A को टिकटें खरीदने के लिए ₹2 और चाहिए।
option_c_hindi: दो टिकट खरीदने के बाद A के पास 50 पैसे बच जाएँगे।
option_d_hindi: A के पास अब जो नकदी है, वह अभी भी दो टिकट खरीदने के लिए पर्याप्त नहीं है।
explanation_english:
Correct Answer: (c) After buying the two tickets A will be left with 50 paise.
Explanation: Let total bus fare for 2 persons be $F$. 
Given $10 = 0.80 \times F \implies F = 10 / 0.8 = ₹12.50$.
Total money A and B have together = ₹10 (A) + ₹3 (B) = ₹13.00.
After buying two tickets, money left = $13.00 - 12.50 = ₹0.50$ (50 paise).
explanation_hindi:
सही उत्तर: (c) दो टिकट खरीदने के बाद A के पास 50 पैसे बच जाएँगे।
स्पष्टीकरण: मान लीजिए दो व्यक्तियों का कुल किराया $F$ है। 
दी गई शर्त के अनुसार: $10 = 0.80 \times F \implies F = ₹12.50$।
A और B के पास कुल राशि = ₹10 + ₹3 = ₹13.00।
किराया चुकाने के बाद शेष राशि = $13.00 - 12.50 = ₹0.50$ (50 पैसे)।

question_english: As per agreement with a bank, a businessman had to refund a loan in some equal instalments without interest. After paying 18 instalments he found that 60 percent of his loan was refunded. How many instalments were there in the agreement?
question_hindi: एक बैंक से किए गए समझौते के अनुसार, एक व्यापारी को कोई ऋणराशि कुछ समान किश्तों में बिना ब्याज चुकानी थी। 18 किश्त चुकाने के बाद उसने पाया कि उसका 60 प्रतिशत ऋण चुक गया। समझौते के अनुसार कितनी किश्तें थीं ?
explanation_english:
Correct Answer: (c) 30
Explanation: Let total instalments be $N$. Each instalment pays an equal fraction of the loan. 
After 18 instalments, fraction paid = $18/N = 60\% = 0.60$.
$18/N = 3/5 \implies 3N = 90 \implies N = 30$.
explanation_hindi:
सही उत्तर: (c) 30
स्पष्टीकरण: मान लीजिए कुल किश्तें $N$ हैं। चूँकि किश्तें समान हैं, 18 किश्तों में चुकाया गया भाग = $18/N = 60\% = 3/5$। 
$18/N = 3/5 \implies 3N = 90 \implies N = 30$।

question_hindi: कोई श्रमिक अपने घर से फैक्टरी तक 5 कि.मी. प्रति घंटा की गति से चलकर अपनी फैक्टरी में 3 मिनट विलंब से पहुँचता है। यदि वह 6 कि.मी. प्रति घंटा की गति से चलता है, तो वह फैक्टरी 7 मिनट पहले पहुँचता है। फैक्टरी से उसके घर की दूरी क्या है ?
explanation_english:
Correct Answer: (c) 5 km
Explanation: Let distance be $D$ km. 
Time taken at 5 km/hr = $D/5$. Time taken at 6 km/hr = $D/6$.
Difference in time = $3 \text{ mins late} - (-7 \text{ mins early}) = 10 \text{ minutes} = 10/60 = 1/6 \text{ hour}$.
$D/5 - D/6 = 1/6 \implies D/30 = 1/6 \implies D = 5 \text{ km}$.
explanation_hindi:
सही उत्तर: (c) 5 कि.मी.
स्पष्टीकरण: मान लीजिए घर से फैक्टरी की दूरी $D$ कि.मी. है। 
समय का अंतर = $3 - (-7) = 10 \text{ मिनट} = 10/60 = 1/6 \text{ घंटे}$।
$D/5 - D/6 = 1/6 \implies D/30 = 1/6 \implies D = 5 \text{ कि.मी.}$।

Directions for the following 7 (seven) items: Read the following two passages and answer the items that follow each passage. Your answers to these items should be based on the passages only.

Passage - 1
Many nations now place their faith in capitalism and governments choose it as the strategy to create wealth for their people. The spectacular economic growth seen in Brazil, China and India after the liberalisation of their economies is proof of its enormous potential and success. However, the global banking crisis and the economic recession have left many bewildered. The debates tend to focus on free market operations and forces, their efficiency and their ability for self correction. Issues of justice, integrity and honesty are rarely elaborated to highlight the failure of the global banking system. The apologists of the system continue to justify the success of capitalism and argue that the recent crisis was a blip.

Their arguments betray an ideological bias with the assumptions that an unregulated market is fair and competent, and that the exercise of private greed will be in the larger public interest.

Few recognize the bidirectional relationship between capitalism and greed; that each reinforces the other. Surely, a more honest conceptualisation of the conflicts of interest among the rich and powerful players who have benefited from the system, their biases and ideology is needed; the focus on the wealth creation should also highlight the resultant gross inequity.

इस परिच्छेद से "निजी लालच का व्यवहार वृहत्तर लोकहित में होगा",

question_english:
According to the passage, what is/are the reason/reasons for saying that the time has come to review the role of public sector?
1. Now public sector has lost its relevance in the industrialization process.
2. Public sector does not perform satisfactorily.
3. Entrepreneurship in private sector is expanding.
4. Effective competition policies are available now.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct in the given context?
question_hindi:
इस परिच्छेद के अनुसार, यह कहने का/के क्या कारण है/हैं कि सार्वजनिक क्षेत्रक की भूमिका के पुनरवलोकन का समय आ गया है ?
1. औद्योगीकरण प्रक्रिया में अब सार्वजनिक क्षेत्रक ने अपनी प्रासंगिकता खो दी है।
2. सार्वजनिक क्षेत्रक संतोषजनक ढंग से निष्पादन नहीं करता।
3. प्राइवेट क्षेत्रक में उद्यमवृत्ति बढ़ रही है।
4. अब प्रभावकारी प्रतियोगी नीतियाँ उपलब्ध हैं।
दिए गए संदर्भ में, उपर्युक्त में से कौन-सा/से कथन सही है/हैं ?
explanation_english:
Correct Answer: (c) 2, 3 and 4 only
Explanation: Statement 2 is correct (less-than-satisfactory performance of public enterprises). Statement 3 is correct (maturing of private sector and expanding entrepreneurship). Statement 4 is correct (growing institutional capabilities to enforce competition policies). Statement 1 is incorrect because the text acknowledges the historic role played in industrialization, not that it completely lost relevance, but that performance and context have evolved.
explanation_hindi:
सही उत्तर: (c) केवल 2, 3 और 4
स्पष्टीकरण: कथन 2 (सार्वजनिक उपक्रमों का संतोषजनक से न्यून निष्पादन), कथन 3 (प्राइवेट क्षेत्रक की परिपक्वता और उद्यमवृत्ति का प्रसार), और कथन 4 (प्रतियोगिता नीतियों को लागू करने के बढ़ते सांस्थानिक सामर्थ्य) सही कारण हैं। कथन 1 गलत है क्योंकि सार्वजनिक क्षेत्र ने औद्योगीकरण में भूमिका निभाई है, पूरी तरह प्रासंगिकता खोने की बात नहीं कही गई है।

इस्पात का ही उदाहरण लें । लगभग शून्य प्रशुल्क के साथ, भारत इस धातु के लिए एक सार्वभौम प्रतियोगी बाज़ार है। भारतीय व्यापार-प्रतिष्ठान विश्व बाज़ार में इस्पात का निर्यात करते हैं, जिससे यह निदर्शित होता है कि प्रौद्योगिकी में कोई अंतराल नहीं है। भारतीय कम्पनियाँ विश्व की इस्पात कम्पनियों को खरीद रही हैं, जो यह दिखाता है कि पूँजी उपलब्धता में कोई अंतराल नहीं है। इन दशाओं में, प्राइवेट स्वामित्व उत्कृष्ट कार्य करता है।

विनियमित उद्योगों में, वित्त से लेकर आधारिक संरचना तक, प्राइवेट स्वामित्व साफ तौर पर वांछनीय है, जहाँ सरकारी अभिकरण विनियमन का कार्य निष्पन्न करे और बहुल प्रतियोगी व्यापार-प्रतिष्ठान प्राइवेट क्षेत्रक में अवस्थित हों। यहाँ, सरल और स्पष्ट समाधान है सरकार का खेलपंच (अम्पायर) की तरह होना और प्राइवेट क्षेत्रक का खिलाड़ियों की तरह होना ही सबसे अच्छी तरह कार्य करता है। इनमें से अनेक उद्योगों में, सरकारी स्वामित्व की विरासत है, जहाँ उत्पादकता की प्रवृत्ति अपेक्षाकृत कम रहने की ओर है, दिवालियेपन का भय मौजूद नहीं है, और करदाताओं से धन की माँग का जोखिम हमेशा बना हुआ है। इसमें सरकार के स्वामी होने और नियामक होने के बीच एक हित-द्वन्द्व भी बना रहता है। यदि सरकारी कम्पनियाँ कार्यरत न हों, तो प्रतियोगिता नीति की रचना और कार्यान्वयन और भी सशक्त और निष्पक्ष होगा।

question_english: The letters L, M, N, O, P, Q, R, S and T in order are substituted by nine integers 1 to 9 but not in that order. 4 is assigned to P. The difference between P and T is 5. The difference between N and T is 3. What is the integer assigned to N?
question_hindi: L, M, N, O, P, Q, R, S और T अक्षरों को नौ पूर्णांकों, 1 से 9 से प्रतिस्थापित किया जाता है, परन्तु उसी क्रम में नहीं। P के लिए 4 निर्धारित है। P और T के बीच अंतर 5 है। N और T के बीच अंतर 3 है। N के लिए निर्धारित पूर्णांक क्या है ?
explanation_english:
Correct Answer: (d) 6
Explanation: Given that $P = 4$. The difference between $P$ and $T$ is 5, so $T$ can be $4 - 5$ (not possible since integers are 1 to 9) or $4 + 5 = 9$. Thus, $T = 9$. The difference between $N$ and $T$ is 3, so $N$ can be $9 - 3 = 6$ or $9 + 3 = 12$ (invalid). Hence, $N = 6$.
explanation_hindi:
सही उत्तर: (d) 6
स्पष्टीकरण: दिया गया है कि $P = 4$ है। $P$ और $T$ का अंतर 5 है, इसलिए $T$ का मान $4 + 5 = 9$ होगा। $N$ और $T$ का अंतर 3 है, इसलिए $N$ का मान $9 - 3 = 6$ होगा।

question_english: Four persons, Alok, Bhupesh, Chander and Dinesh have a total of ₹100 among themselves. Alok and Bhupesh between them have as much money as Chander and Dinesh between them, but Alok has more money than Bhupesh; and Chander has only half the money that Dinesh has. Alok has in fact ₹5 more than Dinesh has. Who has the maximum amount of money?
question_hindi: चार व्यक्तियों - आलोक, भूपेश, चंदर और दिनेश के पास कुल मिलाकर ₹100 हैं। आलोक और भूपेश के पास की धनराशि मिलाकर उतनी ही धनराशि है जितनी चंदर और दिनेश के पास की धनराशि मिलाकर, किन्तु आलोक के पास भूपेश से अधिक धनराशि है; और चंदर के पास दिनेश से केवल आधी धनराशि है। आलोक के पास वस्तुतः दिनेश से ₹5 अधिक हैं। किसके पास अधिकतम धनराशि है ?

Explanation: Let amounts be $A, B, C, D$.

Comparing amounts: Alok ($38.33$) has the maximum amount.

question_english: In a row 'A' is in the $11^{th}$ position from the left and 'B' is in the $10^{th}$ position from the right. If 'A' and 'B' interchange, then 'A' becomes $18^{th}$ from the left. How many persons are there in the row other than 'A' and 'B'?
question_hindi: किसी पंक्ति में 'A' बाईं ओर से 11वें स्थान पर है और 'B' दाहिनी ओर से 10वें स्थान पर है। यदि 'A' और 'B' आपस में स्थान बदल लें, तो 'A' बाईं ओर से 18वें स्थान पर हो जाता है। पंक्ति में 'A' और 'B' के अलावा कितने व्यक्ति हैं ?
explanation_english:
Correct Answer: (c) 25
Explanation: After interchanging, A takes B's position which is $18^{th}$ from the left and also known to be $10^{th}$ from the right. 
Total persons in the row $= \text{Left rank} + \text{Right rank} - 1 = 18 + 10 - 1 = 27$.
Persons other than A and B $= 27 - 2 = 25$.
explanation_hindi:
सही उत्तर: (c) 25
स्पष्टीकरण: स्थान बदलने के बाद A, B के स्थान पर पहुँच जाता है जो बाईं से 18वें और दाईं से 10वें स्थान पर है। 
पंक्ति में कुल व्यक्ति = $18 + 10 - 1 = 27$।
A और B को छोड़कर अन्य व्यक्तियों की संख्या = $27 - 2 = 25$।

question_hindi: B की स्थिति A के उत्तर में है और C की स्थिति A के पूर्व में है। दूरियाँ AB और AC क्रमशः 5 कि.मी. और 12 कि.मी. हैं। B और C स्थानों के बीच की लघुतम दूरी (कि.मी. में) क्या है ?

Explanation: A forms a right-angled triangle with B (North) and C (East). 
Shortest distance $BC = \sqrt{AB² + AC²} = \sqrt{5² + 12²} = \sqrt{25 + 144} = \sqrt{169} = 13 \text{ km}$.

question_english: Two cars start towards each other, from two places A and B which are at a distance of 160 km. They start at the same time 08:10 AM. If the speeds of the cars are 50 km and 30 km per hour respectively, they will meet each other at
question_hindi: 160 कि.मी. दूरी पर स्थित A और B दो स्थानों से दो कारें एक-दूसरे की तरफ प्रस्थान करती हैं। दोनों कारें एक ही समय 08:10 पूर्वाह्न पर प्रस्थान करती हैं। यदि कारों की गति प्रति घंटे क्रमशः 50 कि.मी. और 30 कि.मी. है, तो कारें एक-दूसरे से किस समय पर मिलेंगी ?
explanation_english:
Correct Answer: (a) 10:10 AM
Explanation: Relative speed $= 50 + 30 = 80 \text{ km/h}$. 
Time taken to meet $= \frac{\text{Distance}}{\text{Relative speed}} = \frac{160}{80} = 2 \text{ hours}$. 
Meeting time $= 08:10 \text{ AM} + 2 \text{ hours} = 10:10 \text{ AM}$.
explanation_hindi:

question_english: If the $3^{rd}$ day of a month is Monday, which one of the following will be the fifth day from $21^{st}$ of this month?
question_hindi: यदि किसी माह का तीसरा दिन सोमवार है, तो उसी माह की 21वीं तारीख से पाँचवाँ दिन, निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा होगा ?
explanation_english:
Correct Answer: (c) Wednesday *(Note: Official key is C)*
Explanation: 3rd is Monday $\implies$ 10th, 17th, 24th are Mondays. 
The fifth day from the 21st is $21 + 5 = 26\text{th}$. 
Since 24th is Monday, 25th is Tuesday, and 26th is Wednesday.
explanation_hindi:
सही उत्तर: (c) बुधवार
स्पष्टीकरण: यदि 3 तारीख को सोमवार है, तो 24 तारीख को भी सोमवार होगा। 21वीं तारीख से पाँचवाँ दिन $21 + 5 = 26$ तारीख होगी। चूँकि 24 को सोमवार है, 25 को मंगलवार और 26 तारीख को बुधवार होगा।

question_english: For a charity show, the total tickets sold were 420. Half of these tickets were sold at the rate of ₹5 each, one-third at the rate of ₹3 each and the rest for ₹2 each. What was the total amount received?
question_hindi: किसी चैरिटी शो के लिए, कुल 420 टिकटें बिकीं। इन टिकटों में आधी प्रत्येक ₹5 की दर पर, एक-तिहाई प्रत्येक ₹3 की दर पर और शेष टिकटें प्रत्येक ₹2 की दर पर बिकीं। कुल प्राप्त धनराशि कितनी थी ?
explanation_english:
Correct Answer: (c) ₹1,610
Explanation: Total tickets = 420.
- Half ($210$ tickets) at ₹5 each $= 210 \times 5 = ₹1050$.
- One-third ($140$ tickets) at ₹3 each $= 140 \times 3 = ₹420$.
- Rest ($420 - 210 - 140 = 70$ tickets) at ₹2 each $= 70 \times 2 = ₹140$.
Total amount $= 1050 + 420 + 140 = ₹1,610$.
